raw_response:
I farm the full 14 mu in the usual wheat-maize rotation, so I will put all 14 mu into winter wheat after the autumn sowing and then all 14 mu back into summer maize after wheat harvest. I do not like to gamble on a big change. I will stay close to what works around Quzhou, but I will not cut fertilizer too hard because losing yield hurts more than wasting a little fertilizer. For wheat, I will use an improved variety, rotary till the land after maize, put most of the phosphorus and potassium in as base fertilizer, split the nitrogen between base and topdressing, and give about 3 irrigations with my well if the season is normal. Wheat here needs steady water more than maize. For maize, I will use hybrid seed, keep the wheat stubble and go with no-tillage seeding to save time and labor, put some compound fertilizer at planting, then chase nitrogen at the big flare stage. Summer rain does a lot of the work, so I will plan on 1 irrigation and add a second only if the rain misses us. I will spray wheat about 3 times because weeds, aphids, and disease can all cost money fast, and maize about 2 times for weeds and later insects. With this kind of management on 14 mu, I will aim around 620 kg per mu for wheat and 720 kg per mu for maize. That is a level I feel is worth paying for and still safe on cost.
